correctness.rationale: C: For all \(0<s_1<s_2<s_3\) and \(a,\omega>0\), the explicit strict bound on \(K\) makes \(\beta>0\), each \(I(s_i)>0\), and \(r>\sigma\). Multiplication of the exact nullcline equation yields the cubic \(-a\omega\prod(S-s_i)\), proving exactly three feasible positive equilibria. The Jacobian determinant equals \(a\mu\omega\tau_i\prod_{j\ne i}(s_i-s_j)/(1+\omega s_i)\); its signs are positive, negative, positive, while the chosen bound on \(\mu\) makes both outer traces negative. Real hyperbolicity of the middle equilibrium follows from its negative determinant; sink hyperbolicity follows from positive determinant and negative trace. The quadratic fire-only equation has exactly one positive root as \(r>\sigma\). The implicit function theorem proves the open seven-parameter persistence. Exact rational checker verifies equilibria and Jacobians of an example; no finite computation substitutes for the general proof. No claim is made about full basin structure or periodic orbit absence.

value.rationale: V: Disturbance feedback can cause abrupt switches among ecological states, and the exact motivating article treats single-equilibrium local stability. A constructive realization of *any* triple of positive susceptible densities, with two stable endemic states and a separating endemic saddle despite unique positive fire-only equilibrium, identifies an intrinsic, robust multi-attractor mechanism not captured by a merely algebraic cubic root count. The theorem supplies design inequalities, exact nondegenerate example, and open-parameter persistence that are meaningful to qualitative bifurcation and alternative-stable-state analysis. No ecology-data fit or new general theory of bistability is claimed.
